title: Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) — National Weather Service
claims: WBGT is a heat stress index combining temperature, humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation using measured wet bulb, globe and dry bulb temperatures.
The heat index combines air temperature and relative humidity but does not account for wind speed, cloud cover or radiant heat.
WBGT is used to determine heat-related risk and set rest-work cycles, while wet bulb temperature alone measures the cooling limit through evaporation.
